chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who reviles ʿAlī عليه السلام? He said: So he said to me, “His blood is lawful, by Allah, were it not that you might thereby strike an innocent person.”

He said: I said, then what do you say about a man who harms us? He said: So he said, “In what way is that?” He said: I said, regarding you—he mentions you. He said: So he said to me, “Does he have any share concerning ʿAlī?” I said: He indeed says that and makes it public. He said: “Do not expose yourself to him.”

key_terms.بَرِيئًا: an innocent person, free of guilt
key_terms.تَغْمِزَ: to implicate, strike, or wrongfully target
key_terms.حَلَالُ الدَّمِ: lawful to kill; one whose blood is not protected in this context
key_terms.سَبَّابَةٍ: one who repeatedly insults or reviles
key_terms.لَا تَعَرَّضْ لَهُ: do not confront him or put yourself in his way
key_terms.مُؤْذٍ: harmful; one who causes injury or offense

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about one who openly reviles Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a question to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about one who openly reviles Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and about one who causes harm by speaking against the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. The report presents a severe ruling in principle, while also cautioning against action where it may lead to harming an innocent person or exposing oneself to danger.
